headline: High: shared filesystem writes and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; no critical compliance mismatch is evident.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem, while plano can read config files and send data to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. That creates a plausible file-based injection path if Mentat outputs are placed where plano ingests them. The pair is not documented as isolated, so uncertainty stays above low.
conditions: IF Mentat writes attacker-controlled text into a file that plano later ingests as configuration or prompt material
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace without content provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files by plano
Add a manual review step before plano consumes Mentat outputs
Use read-only mounts for shared inputs where possible
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between file producers and consumers

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code and has broad network egress; plano touches logs, traces, and metrics and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace, code or operational data can flow from one agent into the other and then out to a third-party model endpoint. The profiles do not show hard isolation, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same files or config directory
IF either agent forwards its full context to its model provider during normal operation
mitigations: Keep sensitive code and logs in separate workspaces
Restrict outbound network access for one agent during shared tasks
Redact secrets before either agent processes shared files
Review which files plano loads from config.yaml
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model shares state via filesystem. Plano also reads files and can run multiple instances only if the orchestrator provides it, but no locking is documented. Concurrent edits to the same workspace can corrupt git state or overwrite files, making the default shared-filesystem pairing dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents are allowed to write to the same repository or config tree
IF git operations occur without external locking or merge coordination
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Serialize write access with a lock file
Pause one agent before the other edits git state
Review and merge diffs manually
requires-engineering: add workspace-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and plano can consume files and act through its API-facing gateway role. If plano treats Mentat-generated content as authoritative, errors can cascade from code edits into downstream routing or operational decisions. There is no evidence of a verification barrier between them, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF plano ingests Mentat-produced text without independent validation
IF Mentat outputs are used as inputs to plano-driven routing or automation
mitigations: Require human review of Mentat diffs before reuse
Add schema validation to any Mentat-to-plano handoff
Keep plano from acting on free-form text without checks
Log and compare source inputs against outputs
requires-engineering: insert a verification stage between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only clearly touch source code or agentic telemetry, with no stated residency, HIPAA, or GDPR mismatch. Mentat handles model-provider API keys, but plano lists no secrets or regulated data classes. Because no compliance conflict is documented, this is low rather than none due to incomplete policy detail.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's workspace
IF deployment policy requires a specific residency or retention guarantee not shown in either profile
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared files
Confirm retention settings for the model provider endpoints
Document data-handling boundaries for each agent
Separate logs from source-code workspaces
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
